title: Why Festivals Persist
sentences: Most public celebrations have comfortably outlived the beliefs that produced them.
This is usually described as a decline, which misreads what they were ever really for.
A festival synchronises a population without requiring agreement about anything at all.
The shared date now quietly performs the work that shared conviction used to perform on its own.
That function survives perfectly well after the original meaning has gone.
Attempts to abolish such occasions on rational grounds fail with striking regularity.
Attempts to invent replacements by official decree fail even more reliably than that.
What cannot be legislated is the sense that everybody is doing it at once.
Commerce appears to have understood all of this considerably earlier than governments ever did.
The holiday endures, its explanation quietly replaced every second generation or so.
